newsitem.title: USA: Dozens of homes flooded in San Jose, California.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of homes flooded in San Jose, California.

text.p: Dozens of homes and vehicles were under water in San Jose on Monday after a creek burst its banks and flooded several parts of the city, local officials said.
Water released from Anderson reservoir, brimming over after one of the wettest months on record, charged into Coyote Creek, spilling over at four places in San Jose.
About 4 feet (1.2 metres) of water stood in some city streets, flooding homes and partly submerging cars. Many residents found the best way to get around was by boat.
City spokeswoman Lindsey Wolf said eight homes in one part of town and 30 apartments in another area were flooded and about 200 people had been evacuated.
Damage to public and private property was estimated at about $6 million, she said. The water had also run through five mobile home parks but had not entered homes, she said.
Wolf said the water was receding and officials hoped the creek would retreat back to within its banks by Monday evening.

Northern California enjoyed a break on Monday from the persistent rain that caused devastating flooding earlier this month. The New Year's floods damaged thousands of homes and inundated wide areas of farmland, causing at least $1.5 billion of damage.

Showers were forecast for Monday night but the rest of the week was expected to be dry. But state officials said there was still a danger of levee breaks along the San Joaquin River, a major waterway running through central California.
"We do have a system that is very full. It is still stressed to capacity," Eric Butler, chief of flood center operations for the California Department of Water Resources, said.

Northern California reservoirs are very full and need to release a vast quantity of water to create storage capacity in case of more storms, officials said. But doing so with rivers still running so high creates the threat of flooding downstream.
"We need about a month of dry weather," Butler said. "The odds of getting that are very small."
